summary: The draft covers B07's scope and done_when, keeps the existing tests safe (a race UI without a track id saves nothing, and the results chip still shows this race's best lap), and its overlaps with the open PRs can be resolved. But AC4 hides the NEW BEST chip 3 s (180 ticks) after the lap. Board 05 #3 says the chip slides out (200 ms), holds 2 s and slides back. An append-only test would lock that wrong timing in for good, so the draft needs a revision before it is built.

findings.claim: AC4 and the Summary hide the NEW BEST chip 180 ticks (3 s) after the lap ends. Board 05 Motion (#3 HUD events) says: 'New best: chip slides out from under the timer (200ms), holds 2s, slides back. The timer itself never animates.' AC4 pins the wrong duration into a test that can never be edited.
findings.suggestedFix: Take the timing from the board, in sim ticks worked out from tokens. The chip slides out over tokens.motion.durationMs.slide, holds 2000 ms, then slides back. Rewrite AC4 so the chip is still shown at lapEnd + ceil((slide + 2000) × 60 / 1000) − 1 ticks and hidden by lapEnd + ceil((slide + 2000 + slide) × 60 / 1000) ticks, and is also hidden when a new race starts. The test should compute these numbers from tokens, not write 180 or 3 s. Change the Summary and playtest step 3 to 'about two seconds'.

findings.claim: The draft only says the NEW BEST chip goes 'in the top-right stack under TIME'. The BEST chip already sits tucked under TIME (hud.css .ui-hud-best), so the builder has to guess where the new chip goes and which way it slides. The draft also leaves out the board 05 reduced-motion rule: under prefers-reduced-motion every move except the press becomes a cut.
findings.suggestedFix: Say it is a mustard chip/badge (UI_RULES §10), built like .ui-hud-best (no top outline, square top corners). It tucks under the BEST chip (the timer stack) and slides down out from behind it with a transform only (slide 200 ms, snap easing), then slides back. Under prefers-reduced-motion it appears and disappears without moving. The TIME panel itself never moves.

findings.claim: AC4's position check ('in the top-right stack under TIME') can't be observed in happy-dom, which has no layout. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7 also pin the storage key 'racer.bestLap.<trackId>' and its millisecond format forever. That is acceptable as a persistence format (B08 and B11 will read it), but it has to be deliberate.
findings.suggestedFix: In AC4, test that the chip exists in the HUD by its text 'NEW BEST' and is visible or hidden. Leave the position to the screen stages and screenshots, or to a browser test via harness/screens/browser.ts. Keep the storage key as a deliberate, documented format: one exported constant or function in best-laps.ts that B08 and B11 reuse.

findings.claim: #24 (B05, desktop HUD) also edits hud.ts and hud.css. A new chip added under the timer will need the ×1.45 desktop sizing that #24 brings, so whichever PR merges second has to size the chip for desktop or adopt the other's layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Size the new chip only through the same CSS variables and classes the BEST chip uses (.ui-hud-best and the outline and space tokens), so B05's desktop scaling covers it without changes. Keep the hud.ts edit to adding one element inside .ui-hud__timer plus one show/hide method.

overlapAssessment: #23 changes game.ts only in draw() and the driver step loop (camera framing). B07 only passes the track id and stored best to ui.reset() at race start, on different lines. #25 (gamepad, diff not in /inputs) per its summary edits game.ts input polling, which is unrelated. #24 (desktop HUD, diff not in /inputs) changes HUD sizes in a desktop mode. B07 adds one chip element and its show/hide, and neither builds on the other. The risk is a textual conflict in the timer markup and CSS, which goes away if the chip reuses the BEST chip's classes and tokens. Safe to build now.
backlogChangeRequests: B07 scope could cite board 05 #3 (chip slides out 200 ms, holds 2 s, slides back) next to UI_RULES §7, so future drafts take the hold time from the board rather than inventing one.
